workload.state: Fresh private synthetic state with the packaged SQLite and verified sqlite-vec configuration.
workload.activity: Idle Core service, with a public client-protocol readiness and health probe every 60 seconds, including interval endpoints.

metric_definitions.installed_core_artifact_bytes: Uncompressed Core executable plus every required packaged asset, including manifest, service configuration and any external SQLite engine; embedded bytes counted once; measurement tools excluded.
metric_definitions.startup_seconds: Monotonic elapsed time from requesting service start to a correlated protocol response proving recovery completed, including service-manager and measurement-launcher overhead.
metric_definitions.peak_resident_bytes: Maximum OS resident high-water mark for the Core process from process start through final shutdown; initialization included, physical footprint and monitor RSS excluded.
metric_definitions.mean_cpu_percent: 100 times the Core user-plus-system CPU counter delta divided by the complete post-readiness residency interval; health-probe work included.
metric_definitions.max_cpu_window_percent: At most five percent in any rolling 60-second window during residency, evaluated at every one-second resource sample using actual elapsed time; no division by CPU count.

rationale: A 64 MiB installed Core target bounds distribution cost; a two-second readiness target bounds service startup; 256 MiB leaves room for Go and the SQLite engine while retaining a bounded resident service; one percent mean idle CPU and five percent per minute detect sustained idle activity. These are pre-run acceptance targets, not measurements.
failure_policy: Missing platform evidence, missing or invalid counters, excessive sampling gaps, missed or failed health probes, restarts, suspension, changed artifacts, or a short run prevent acceptance. An exceeded limit is a failed result and reopens the runtime choice; limits are not increased after observing a run.
